subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following organic compounds is held together by HYDROGEN BONDS as its strongest intermolecular force?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Pentanoic acid (carboxylic acid) has an –OH group capable of forming hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen bonding is the strongest of the listed IMFs.

subQuestions.questionText: To which HOMOLOGOUS SERIES does a compound with molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₂ belong?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
CnH(2n)O₂ is the general formula for carboxylic acids (and esters). C₆H₁₂O₂ fits CnH2nO2 for n=6.

subQuestions.questionText: Which TWO functional groups are needed to form an ESTER?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Esterification: carboxylic acid (–COOH = carboxyl) reacts with alcohol (–OH = hydroxyl) to form an ester and water.

subQuestions.questionText: A yellow CrO₄²⁻ solution turns orange. Which ONE caused this change?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
2CrO₄²⁻(yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻(orange) + H₂O. Adding acid (H⁺) shifts equilibrium to products (orange). HCl provides H⁺.

subQuestions.questionText:
In a potential energy diagram, the reactants are at energy level P, the activated complex at Q, and the products at R (R < P). What is the ACTIVATION ENERGY for the forward reaction?

*(Refer to the energy diagram in the original question paper.)*
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Activation energy for forward reaction = energy of activated complex − energy of reactants = Q − P.

subQuestions.questionText: The reaction 3H₂(g) + N₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) is exothermic. Which ONE of the following will INCREASE Kc?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Kc only changes with temperature. For exothermic reaction, DECREASING temperature (cooling) shifts equilibrium to products side, INCREASING Kc.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which TWO of the following statements about the ionisation of H₂SO₄ are CORRECT?

I. H₂SO₄ is a strong acid.
II. H₂SO₄ ionises completely in the first step.
III. H₂SO₄ ionises completely in both steps.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
H₂SO₄ is a strong acid (I). It ionises completely in the FIRST step (→ H⁺ + HSO₄⁻) but incompletely in the second step (HSO₄⁻ is a weak acid). So I and II only.

subQuestions.questionText: In which ONE of the following electrochemical cells will the VOLTMETER show a POSITIVE reading?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
For spontaneous cell: stronger reducing agent at anode. Cu is stronger reducing agent than Ag (E°_Cu = +0.34V, E°_Ag = +0.80V). Cu is oxidised at anode, Ag⁺ reduced at cathode. E_cell = E_cathode − E_anode > 0.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following is CORRECT about an ELECTROLYTIC cell?

options.A: The anode is the positive electrode.
options.B: The cathode is the positive electrode.
options.D: It converts electrical energy to chemical energy spontaneously.

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
In electrolytic cells, the anode is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply (positive electrode). Oxidation occurs at the anode.

subQuestions.questionText: In which process is AMMONIA a REACTANT and in which is it a PRODUCT?

options.A: Product in Ostwald; reactant in Haber
options.B: Reactant in Ostwald; product in Haber

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Haber process: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ (NH₃ is a PRODUCT). Ostwald process: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (NH₃ is a REACTANT).

subQuestions.questionText: Compounds A–F are given. Which letter represents a KETONE?
subQuestions.memoText: Identify the compound with a carbonyl group (C=O) in the middle of the carbon chain (not at the end). (1 mark — letter from diagram.)

subQuestions.questionText: Which TWO compounds are FUNCTIONAL ISOMERS of each other?
subQuestions.memoText: Functional isomers have the same molecular formula but different functional groups (e.g., aldehyde and ketone, or carboxylic acid and ester). Identify from the given structures. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which compound is a HYDROCARBON?
subQuestions.memoText: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen atoms. Identify from the given structures. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: To which HOMOLOGOUS SERIES does compound D belong?
subQuestions.memoText: Identify the functional group of D and state the homologous series (e.g., alkane, alkene, alcohol, aldehyde, ketone, carboxylic acid, ester). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound D.
subQuestions.memoText: Follow IUPAC rules: identify longest chain, number from end nearest substituent/functional group, name substituents as prefixes, name functional group as suffix. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of a POSITIONAL ISOMER of compound F.
subQuestions.memoText: Positional isomer: same molecular formula, same functional group, different position of the functional group on the carbon chain. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of a CHAIN ISOMER of compound F.
subQuestions.memoText: Chain isomer: same molecular formula, same functional group, different carbon skeleton (branched vs straight chain). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Compounds A and E react to form an ester. Write the IUPAC NAME of the organic product.
subQuestions.memoText: Esterification product name: alkyl alkanoate. Name the alcohol part first (as alkyl), then the acid part (as alkanoate). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of the functional group of the ester product.
subQuestions.memoText: Ester functional group: –C(=O)–O– (ester linkage / –COO–). Draw this group in context. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: C₁₀H₂₂ is cracked to form compounds P and Q. What TYPE of reaction is cracking?
subQuestions.memoText: Cracking is a DECOMPOSITION reaction (also acceptable: thermal decomposition / pyrolysis). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: If P is a 3-carbon alkene, write the MOLECULAR FORMULA of Q.
subQuestions.memoText: C₁₀H₂₂ → P(C₃H₆) + Q. Q: C₁₀H₂₂ − C₃H₆ = C₇H₁₆ (heptane). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of compound P (3-carbon alkene).
subQuestions.memoText: P = propene: CH₂=CH–CH₃. Draw structural formula showing all bonds and atoms. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define VAPOUR PRESSURE.
subQuestions.memoText: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by the vapour above a liquid when the rate of evaporation equals the rate of condensation (at equilibrium). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: In the vapour pressure experiment with Butan-1-ol, Butan-2-one and Propanoic acid, what is the INDEPENDENT VARIABLE?
subQuestions.memoText: Temperature. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From the graph, which compound (A = Butan-2-one or B = Butan-1-ol) has the HIGHER vapour pressure at a given temperature?
subQuestions.memoText: Butan-2-one (A) has the higher vapour pressure. It has weaker IMFs (dipole-dipole, no H-bonding) so more molecules escape. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain with reference to INTERMOLECULAR FORCES why the two compounds in 3.3 have different vapour pressures.
subQuestions.memoText: Butan-1-ol has hydrogen bonding (–OH group) as its strongest IMF. Butan-2-one only has dipole-dipole forces. Hydrogen bonds are stronger than dipole-dipole forces. More energy is needed to overcome H-bonds in butan-1-ol → fewer molecules escape → lower vapour pressure. Butan-2-one has weaker IMFs → more molecules in vapour phase → higher vapour pressure. (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the TERM for the temperature X on the vapour pressure graph where vapour pressure = atmospheric pressure?
subQuestions.memoText: Boiling point. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: At point Y on the graph (above the boiling point curve), what PHASE is the substance in?
subQuestions.memoText: Gas/vapour phase. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Sketch the vapour pressure curve for Propanoic acid (C) relative to curve A (Butan-2-one) on the graph.
subQuestions.memoText: Propanoic acid curve C must be BELOW curve A at all temperatures. Propanoic acid has hydrogen bonding (–COOH group, stronger than butan-2-one dipole-dipole). Stronger IMFs → lower vapour pressure → curve below A. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Propane undergoes Step 1 to form compound X (a haloalkane). State the CONDITION required for Step 1 (halogenation of propane).
subQuestions.memoText: UV light / sunlight. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the INORGANIC PRODUCT formed in Step 1?
subQuestions.memoText: HBr (hydrobromic acid). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: X reacts with aqueous NaOH in Step 2 to form propan-2-ol. What TYPE of substitution reaction is Step 2?
subQuestions.memoText: Hydrolysis / nucleophilic substitution. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the INORGANIC REAGENT used in Step 2.
subQuestions.memoText: Dilute/aqueous NaOH (sodium hydroxide solution). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound X.
subQuestions.memoText: 2-bromopropane. (Bromine adds to the middle carbon of propane; more stable product via Markovnikov for unsaturated, but propane halogenation gives mixture; the product that yields propan-2-ol via substitution is 2-bromopropane.) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Ethane can be obtained from chloroethane in TWO steps. Write BALANCED EQUATIONS (using structural formulae) for each step.
subQuestions.memoText: Step 1: Elimination — CH₃CH₂Cl + KOH(alc) → CH₂=CH₂ + KCl + H₂O. (Dehydrohalogenation, alcoholic KOH.) Step 2: Addition/Hydrogenation — CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃. (Nickel catalyst, heat.) (8 marks: 4 per equation)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the RATE OF A CHEMICAL REACTION.
subQuestions.memoText: The rate of a chemical reaction is the change in concentration of reactants or products per unit time. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Al₂(CO₃)₃ reacts with HCl. What MEASUREMENTS would you take to DETERMINE the rate of this reaction?
subQuestions.memoText: Measure the volume of CO₂ gas produced over time / measure the mass of the reaction flask over time (as CO₂ escapes, mass decreases). Record volume or mass at regular time intervals. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Experiment I uses 100 cm³ of 1.5 mol/dm³ HCl; Experiment II uses 50 cm³ of 2 mol/dm³ HCl with the same mass of Al₂(CO₃)₃. Use COLLISION THEORY to explain which experiment has a HIGHER initial rate.
subQuestions.memoText: Experiment II has the higher initial rate. Higher concentration (2 mol/dm³ vs 1.5 mol/dm³) means more particles per unit volume. More frequent collisions between reactant particles. More collisions per unit time with sufficient energy (≥ Ea). Therefore higher reaction rate. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The rate of the reaction is 4.4 × 10⁻³ mol/min. Calculate the MOLES of Al₂(CO₃)₃ remaining after 2.5 minutes. (Initial moles of Al₂(CO₃)₃ = calculated from HCl.)
subQuestions.memoText: Moles HCl = c×V = 1.5×0.1 = 0.15 mol. Al₂(CO₃)₃ + 6HCl → ... Moles Al₂(CO₃)₃ initially = 0.15/6 = 0.025 mol. Moles Al₂(CO₃)₃ reacted in 2.5 min = rate × t = 4.4×10⁻³ × 2.5 = 0.011 mol. Remaining = 0.025 − 0.011 = 0.014 mol. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MAXIMUM VOLUME of CO₂ produced at 25°C. (Molar volume at 25°C = 24 000 cm³/mol.)
subQuestions.memoText: Al₂(CO₃)₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3CO₂ + 3H₂O. Moles Al₂(CO₃)₃ = 0.025 mol. Moles CO₂ = 0.025 × 3 = 0.075 mol. Volume = n × Vm = 0.075 × 24000 = 1800 cm³. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define CHEMICAL EQUILIBRIUM.
subQuestions.memoText: Chemical equilibrium is the state in a reversible reaction when the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction and the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: For 2HI(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + I₂(g), a concentration-time graph shows two curves X and Y. Which curve (X or Y) represents the PRODUCTS? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: The curve that INCREASES then becomes constant represents products. HI (reactant) decreases. H₂ and I₂ (products) increase. The curve for products starts at 0 (or lower) and rises to equilibrium concentration. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: At t = 4 min (before equilibrium), is the RATE OF THE FORWARD REACTION greater than, equal to, or less than the rate of the reverse reaction?
subQuestions.memoText: Greater than. Before equilibrium is reached, the forward rate exceeds the reverse rate (system is still moving towards equilibrium). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Kc = 0.04 for 2HI(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + I₂(g). The container is 500 cm³. Initial [HI] = 1 mol/dm³. Calculate the MOLES OF I₂ at equilibrium (t = 6 min).
subQuestions.memoText: Kc = [H₂][I₂]/[HI]² = 0.04. Let x = moles/dm³ of H₂ (and I₂) formed. [HI] at eq = 1 − 2x. Kc = x²/(1−2x)² = 0.04. √0.04 = x/(1−2x) = 0.2. x = 0.2(1−2x) = 0.2 − 0.4x. 1.4x = 0.2. x = 0.1429 mol/dm³. Moles I₂ = x × V = 0.1429 × 0.5 = 0.0714 mol. (9 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: At t = 10 min on the graph, a change is made that increases the rate of the REVERSE reaction more than the forward reaction. Which reaction is favoured?
subQuestions.memoText: The REVERSE reaction is favoured. The system shifts to produce more reactants (HI). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Is the change at t = 10 min an INCREASE or DECREASE in temperature? Use Le Chatelier's principle and the graph to justify.
subQuestions.memoText: The reverse reaction being favoured means the system absorbs more energy in the reverse direction. If the forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH < 0), then the reverse is endothermic. Increasing temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) reaction. So temperature was INCREASED. This decreases Kc (consistent if graph shows [HI] increasing). (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the term for a solution of known concentration used in titration?
subQuestions.memoText: Standard solution. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: 2 g of NaOH is dissolved in 250 cm³ of solution. Calculate the CONCENTRATION of the NaOH solution.
Calculate the pH of the NaOH solution.

1.5 g of impure CaCO₃ is added to excess HCl. The excess HCl is then neutralised by 25 cm³ of the 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH solution. Calculate the INITIAL CONCENTRATION of the HCl solution. (Assume HCl volume = 40 cm³.)
subQuestions.memoText: Moles NaOH = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005 mol. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O (1:1). Moles HCl (excess) = 0.005 mol. CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Moles CaCO₃ = (purity factor × 1.5)/100 g/mol. Need purity for exact answer. Total moles HCl = moles reacted with CaCO₃ + excess. [HCl] = total moles / 0.040. (8 marks — full calculation.)

subQuestions.questionText: Define REDUCTION in terms of electrons.
subQuestions.memoText: Reduction is the GAIN of electrons by a species / a decrease in oxidation state. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the REDUCTION HALF-REACTION for sodium reacting with water.
subQuestions.memoText: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ (or 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the overall BALANCED EQUATION for sodium reacting with water.
subQuestions.memoText: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The solution turns PINK with phenolphthalein after Na reacts with water. Why?
subQuestions.memoText: NaOH (a strong base) is produced. The solution is alkaline (pH > 7). Phenolphthalein turns pink in alkaline conditions. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does COPPER NOT REACT with water?
subQuestions.memoText: Copper is a weaker reducing agent than hydrogen. E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V is positive, meaning Cu is not easily oxidised. Cu cannot reduce water (H₂O) to H₂ because Cu is less reactive than hydrogen / Cu is below hydrogen in the activity series. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What does a SINGLE LINE (|) represent in cell notation?
subQuestions.memoText: A single line represents a phase boundary / an interface between two phases (e.g., solid electrode and solution). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the ENERGY CONVERSION in a galvanic cell.
subQuestions.memoText: Chemical (potential) energy is converted to electrical energy. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the EMF of the cell: Pb|Pb²⁺ || Fe³⁺, Fe²⁺ | Pt. (E°(Pb²⁺/Pb) = −0.13 V; E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V.)
subQuestions.memoText: E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode = +0.77 − (−0.13) = +0.90 V. (Pb is anode: oxidised. Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ is cathode: Fe³⁺ reduced.) (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Are cells A and B (CuCl₂(aq) and Al₂O₃(l) with external power supply) ELECTROLYTIC or GALVANIC cells? Justify.
subQuestions.memoText: ELECTROLYTIC cells. They require an external power supply (do not produce electrical energy spontaneously). Non-spontaneous reactions are driven by electrical energy. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the ANODE HALF-REACTION in Cell A (CuCl₂(aq), carbon electrodes).
subQuestions.memoText: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ (oxidation of chloride ions at anode). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the CATHODE HALF-REACTION in Cell B (Al₂O₃(l)).
subQuestions.memoText: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al (reduction of aluminium ions at cathode). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the PRODUCT formed at the cathode in Cell A (CuCl₂(aq))?
subQuestions.memoText: Copper (Cu) / copper metal. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In Cell A, why does the MASS of electrode Y DECREASE during electrolysis?
subQuestions.memoText: If Y is the carbon anode: it is oxidised. In CuCl₂(aq) with carbon electrodes, the anode material (carbon) is oxidised over time OR: Cl₂ gas is produced at anode, which does not add mass. Actually for carbon electrodes, anode loses mass due to oxidation. Accept: anode is oxidised / particles leave the anode. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In the Contact process for making H₂SO₄, what is COMPOUND A (the raw material sulfur compound)?
subQuestions.memoText: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂). (Sulfur is burned: S + O₂ → SO₂.) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is COMPOUND B (the intermediate product in Step II of the Contact process)?
subQuestions.memoText: Sulfur trioxide (SO₃). (2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃ in the presence of V₂O₅ catalyst.) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the CATALYST used in Step II of the Contact process?
subQuestions.memoText: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write a BALANCED EQUATION for the reaction of H₂SO₄ with NH₃ to form ammonium sulphate.
subQuestions.memoText: H₂SO₄ + 2NH₃ → (NH₄)₂SO₄. Balanced: 1 H₂SO₄ + 2 NH₃ → 1 (NH₄)₂SO₄. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What does the NPK on a fertiliser bag represent?
subQuestions.memoText: N = nitrogen, P = phosphorus, K = potassium. These are the three main macronutrients in the fertiliser. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A fertiliser bag has NPK 1-3-2 with 26% nitrogen content from NH₄NO₃. How much of this fertiliser is needed to provide 4 kg of NH₄NO₃?
subQuestions.memoText: Wait: re-read: 'mass of fertiliser if it contains 4 kg NH₄NO₃ and N content = 26%.' M(NH₄NO₃) = 80 g/mol. % N in NH₄NO₃ = 28/80 × 100 = 35%. If fertiliser has 26% N and the N comes from NH₄NO₃: 4 kg NH₄NO₃ contains 4×0.35 = 1.4 kg N. Mass fertiliser = 1.4/0.26 = 5.38 kg. (4 marks)
